newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans tumble as hike in U.S. output cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans tumble as hike in U.S. output cited.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures dropped nearly the 30 cent per bushel limit by midsession on a hike in a government estimate for 1996 U.S. soybean production, traders said.
"The numbers set the tone for the market today and beans are acting like they should, there are too many beans," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

USDA early Friday said 1996 U.S. soybean production would total 2.346 billion bushels, above an average trade estimate for 2.287 billion and above the government's forecast in September for 2.270 billion bushels.

USDA also increased to 195 million bushels its forecast for U.S. 1996-97 U.S. ending stocks of soybeans from the September outlook for 160 million bushels. The 1996-97 marketing year ends on August 31, 1997.

Fund selling totaled at least 12.0 million bushels with Refco Inc a featured seller of four million bushels of November, the traders said. Smith Barney, Iowa Grain and Tenco Inc each sold from two to three million bushels, traders said.
At 1114 CDT, soybeans were 13-1/4 to 25 cents per bushel lower, with November down 24-1/4 at $7.06. January was 25 cents lower at $7.12.
Technicians said sell stops were triggered on the open when November broke below chart support at roughly $7.20 per bushel, a support leve since it was near a low for the recent move.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November was below oversold status as of 1117 CDT at 17.807 points, down from the 20 area which is generally considered a very oversold level.
